questions.text: Which two imaging sensor types are explicitly mentioned in the lecture notes?
questions.feedback: The lecture mentions Charged Coupled Device (CCD) and Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS).

questions.text: A histogram tells exactly where each gray level is located in the image.
questions.feedback: A histogram does not preserve where pixels are located.

questions.text: According to the lecture, why does classical DIP still matter for modern AI?
options: DIP prevents all model errors automatically
Only text data matters in AI
AI models follow Garbage In, Garbage Out; poor image input can produce poor outputs
questions.answer: AI models follow Garbage In, Garbage Out; poor image input can produce poor outputs
questions.feedback: The lecture emphasizes that poor input data leads to poor model performance.

questions.text: The lecture notes connect GPUs with improved processing time and modern deep learning.
questions.feedback: GPUs are presented as originally for graphics but now driving deep learning due to parallelism.

questions.text: Match each area with its description from the lecture notes.

pairs.definition: Processes an image and transforms it into an abstract description
Generation of image from non-pictorial information
Both input and output are images

questions.text: Type 1 operations depend on:
options: neighboring pixels as well as the current pixel
questions.answer: neighboring pixels as well as the current pixel
questions.feedback: The lecture says Type 1 operations use neighboring pixel intensities; filtering and edge detection are examples.

questions.text: Object segmentation is the process of:
options: subdividing an image into meaningful disjoint regions
questions.answer: subdividing an image into meaningful disjoint regions
questions.feedback: This matches the lecture definition of segmentation.

questions.text: HSV helps separate true color from illumination information.
questions.feedback: The lecture explains Hue, Saturation, and Value separate color information from illumination.

questions.text: Which is an example of a Type 2 operation from the lecture?
questions.feedback: Type 2 operations include geometric transformations such as rotation, translation, scaling, and reflection.

questions.text: The lecture notes say digital processing is slower than analog processing, but:
questions.feedback: The lecture states digital processing is slower, but manipulation is easy.

questions.text: Why do sensor differences matter for AI, according to the lecture?
options: Models may fail if deployment images differ from training images
Only analog images can train AI
Sensors have no impact on AI models
questions.answer: Models may fail if deployment images differ from training images
questions.feedback: The lecture explains that models can struggle if training and deployment image distributions differ.

questions.text: CCD stands for Charged Coupled ___.
questions.feedback: CCD means Charged Coupled Device.

questions.text: Image acquisition bridges the physical world and the digital realm.
questions.feedback: This sentence appears directly in the lecture notes.

questions.text: One advantage of analog processing mentioned in the lecture is that it is:
questions.feedback: The lecture states analog processing is very fast because A/D and D/A conversion time is saved.

questions.text: Spatial resolution is mainly determined by:
questions.feedback: The lecture says sampling is the principal factor determining spatial resolution.

questions.text: An image histogram is a graphical representation of:
options: intensity distribution in a digital image
questions.answer: intensity distribution in a digital image
questions.feedback: The lecture defines image histogram this way.

questions.text: The lecture states that CCD and CMOS sensors have identical effects on AI performance.
questions.feedback: The lecture emphasizes that sensor differences matter for AI.

questions.text: Image acquisition converts visual information from the real world into:
options: a digital format processed by computers
questions.answer: a digital format processed by computers
questions.feedback: This is directly stated in the lecture notes.

questions.text: Which sequence best matches the image acquisition steps in the lecture?
options: Light sensing, signal analog-to-digital conversion, image formation
questions.answer: Light sensing, signal analog-to-digital conversion, image formation
questions.feedback: These three steps are explicitly listed in the lecture notes.

questions.text: According to the lecture notes, Computer Vision is a field of AI and Computer Science that trains computers to:
options: interpret and understand the visual world
questions.answer: interpret and understand the visual world
questions.feedback: The lecture defines Computer Vision as training computers to interpret and understand the visual world.

questions.text: In h(rk) = nk, nk represents:
options: the number of pixels having gray level rk
questions.answer: the number of pixels having gray level rk
questions.feedback: The lecture states nk is the number of pixels with gray level rk.

questions.text: According to the lecture trade-off, CCD is suitable when:
options: speed and power efficiency are always more important
image quality is more important than speed
questions.answer: image quality is more important than speed
questions.feedback: The lecture notes CCD for scientific AI/medical diagnosis where image quality is prioritized.

questions.text: The lecture states that digital processing is always faster than analog processing.
questions.feedback: The lecture states analog processing is very fast, while digital processing is slower but easier to manipulate.

questions.text: Image resolution depends on:
options: the number of objects inside the image
questions.feedback: The lecture states that resolution depends on sampling and gray levels.

questions.text: A bigger sampling rate improves the approximation of a digitized image.
questions.feedback: The lecture states that bigger sampling rate and gray scale improve approximation.

questions.text: Contrast Stretching improves contrast by:
options: stretching the range of intensity values to cover the whole dynamic range
questions.answer: stretching the range of intensity values to cover the whole dynamic range
questions.feedback: This is the lecture definition of Contrast Stretching.

questions.text: Spatial resolution is mainly determined by ___.
questions.feedback: The lecture states sampling is the principal factor determining spatial resolution.

questions.text: Match each enhancement concept with its lecture meaning.

pairs.definition: Stretches intensity values to cover the whole dynamic range

questions.text: The lecture argues that deep learning is not a replacement for classical image processing foundations.
questions.feedback: The lecture presents deep learning as built on or supported by classical image processing ideas.
